attrs.label: Financial content has no room for error
attrs.html:
Financial content has no room for error

Money decisions are high stakes, for your readers and for your regulator. Pick a challenge to see how we handle it.

The challengeBanks have had a century to earn trust. A newer fintech has to earn it on the page, quickly.

Our approach

Earn trust with clarity, expertise and proof on every page.

People are careful with money, and more careful with a name they don’t know. Every page has to answer the quiet question: can I trust these people with my money?

In practice

  • Expert authors with their experience shown on every piece
  • Clear pages on regulation and how money is protected
  • Fee pages with worked examples
  • Customer stories with real numbers, approved by compliance

Why it matters

Trust is the product in financial services. Content is where people decide whether to give it.

Methods we use

  1. 1Named expert authors

    Bylines from your finance experts, with their experience shown.

  2. 2Safety explained

    How money is protected and how you’re regulated, in plain words.

  3. 3Fee pages in plain words

    Every fee, with worked examples, and no small print surprises.

  4. 4Customer proof

    Stories, reviews and numbers, approved for publication.

What you get

  • Trust pages
  • Expert bylines
  • Customer stories

The challengeDrafts bounce between marketing, compliance and legal for weeks, and timely ideas go stale.

Our approach

Build content for review from the first brief, so sign-off takes days.

Most financial content isn’t slow because of writing. It’s slow because of review. So we design the process around your compliance team from day one.

In practice

  • We agree a claims library and the required warnings before any writing starts
  • Every draft comes with a source log
  • Reviewers get clean copy with tracked changes
  • Time-sensitive pieces follow a fast-track route agreed in advance

Why it matters

When approvals take days, you can publish when it matters, not three months later.

Methods we use

  1. 1A claims library

    What you can and can’t say, agreed with compliance once.

  2. 2A source log

    Every figure and claim linked to its source.

  3. 3Reviewer-ready drafts

    Clean copy, tracked changes and the right warnings in place.

  4. 4A fast-track route

    A pre-agreed process for time-sensitive commentary.

What you get

  • A claims library
  • Source logs
  • Faster approvals

The challengeBig comparison sites and banks take the top results for almost every money question.

Our approach

Win the specific questions they answer badly, and show up where buyers compare.

You won’t outrank a comparison site for “best business account”. But you can own hundreds of specific questions they answer in one line, or not at all.

In practice

  • Research into the exact questions your customers ask
  • Detailed explainers for one type of customer at a time
  • Accurate listings on the comparison sites buyers use
  • Answers structured so AI tools can quote them

Why it matters

Specific questions bring in readers who are closer to choosing a provider.

Methods we use

  1. 1Question research

    The exact questions your customers ask, which big sites answer generically.

  2. 2Niche explainers

    Detailed answers for one type of customer, such as freelancers or importers.

  3. 3Comparison site listings

    Your product listed and described accurately where people compare.

  4. 4Answers AI can quote

    Clear, sourced answers that AI tools pick up and cite.

What you get

  • A search gap map
  • Niche explainers
  • Comparison listings

The challengeFees, rates, eligibility and risk are hard to explain without jargon, or without leaving out what matters.

Our approach

Make the product easy to understand, without making it vague.

Financial products are complicated, and rules often say what you must include. The job is to make it clear without leaving anything out.

In practice

  • Worked examples with real numbers in every product explainer
  • A glossary that every page links to
  • Simple diagrams of how money moves
  • A reading age check on every piece

Why it matters

When people understand a product, they’re more likely to apply, and less likely to complain later.

Methods we use

  1. 1Worked examples

    Real numbers that show what a customer pays and gets.

  2. 2Plain-words glossary

    Every term explained once, and linked from every page.

  3. 3Diagrams and flows

    How money moves, shown in simple pictures.

  4. 4Reading age checks

    Every piece checked so it reads easily.

What you get

  • Worked examples
  • A glossary
  • Simple diagrams

The challengeOne rate change or new rule can make dozens of pages wrong overnight, and wrong financial content is a risk.

Our approach

Track every number and rule, and update content the day it changes.

Rates, fees and rules change all the time. A page with an old rate isn’t just out of date, it can be a compliance problem.

In practice

  • A register of every rate, fee and rule, and where it appears
  • A review date on every piece
  • Same-day updates when something changes
  • A log of every change, ready for audits

Why it matters

Up-to-date content protects you, and keeps the pages that bring in leads working.

Methods we use

  1. 1A fact register

    Every rate, fee and rule, and the pages that mention it.

  2. 2Review dates

    Every piece rechecked on a schedule.

  3. 3Change alerts

    When a number changes, we know which pages to update.

  4. 4An update log

    A record of every change, for your compliance team.

What you get

  • A fact register
  • Same-day updates
  • An audit trail

The challengeMore people ask AI tools about money. They quote sources they trust, and skip the rest.

Our approach

Be the source AI tools quote, with clear, sourced and current answers.

People now ask AI tools “is this account safe?” or “how does invoice finance work?”. Those tools quote a few trusted sources. You want to be one of them.

In practice

  • Answers in the first lines of every page
  • Original numbers only you can publish
  • Named expert authors and clear sources
  • Monthly checks of which AI tools quote you

Why it matters

AI answers are the new first page of search, and they favour sources that show their expertise.

Methods we use

  1. 1Answer-first pages

    The answer in the first lines, then the detail.

  2. 2Original data

    Numbers AI tools can only get from you.

  3. 3Expert authors and sources

    Clear signs that a real expert stands behind each page.

  4. 4Citation tracking

    We check which AI tools quote you, and for what.

What you get

  • Answer-first pages
  • Data pages
  • AI citation reports

The challengeExplainers bring in traffic, but readers leave without opening an account or booking a demo.

Our approach

Give every piece a next step that fits where the reader is.

Explainers are where people learn. But if a reader finishes a great guide and has nowhere to go next, the work stops at traffic.

In practice

  • A calculator or checker linked from every relevant piece
  • Application pages that answer “what do I need?”
  • Reports and guides worth an email address
  • Nurture emails approved by compliance in advance

Why it matters

The same traffic brings in more applications when every piece has a clear next step.

Methods we use

  1. 1Calculators and checkers

    Tools that answer “how much?” and lead to an application.

  2. 2Application-ready pages

    Eligibility, documents needed and time to open, on one page.

  3. 3Downloads

    Guides, templates and reports, in exchange for an email.

  4. 4Nurture emails

    Approved email sequences for people not ready yet.

What you get

  • Calculators
  • Lead magnets
  • Nurture emails
